title: ComingSoonState
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with MonarchBadge, MonarchEmptyState and MonarchText
summary: A placeholder for a feature that is planned but not available yet: a "Coming soon" badge, MonarchEmptyState with the feature and an optional action, and a short list of what is planned.
whenToUse: In a tab, a card or a screen of a feature that is announced but not built yet, so people know it is planned rather than broken or empty.
whenNotToUse: For a feature that exists but has no data yet, use MonarchEmptyState. For a feature the plan does not include, use an upgrade prompt.
api: Column { MonarchBadge(text = "Coming soon", tone = MonarchTone.Info); MonarchEmptyState(title = feature, message = description, actions = { MonarchButton(text = "Notify me", onClick = …) }); highlights.forEach { MonarchText(text = "• $it") } }

options.name: MonarchBadge.text
options.description: "Coming soon", in the app's strings. Leave the badge out when the screen title already says it.

options.name: MonarchEmptyState.title
options.description: The name of the feature, "Status pages", or "Coming soon" when there is no name.

options.name: MonarchEmptyState.message
options.description: What the feature will do, in one sentence.

options.name: MonarchEmptyState.actions
options.description: An optional action, such as "Notify me".

options.name: highlights
options.description: A short list of what is planned, one MonarchText per line, under a heading such as "What is planned".

states.name: planned
states.description: The badge, the feature, its description and the action.

states.name: notified
states.description: After "Notify me" the app disables the button and changes its label.

appearance: The info badge above MonarchEmptyState in its own appearance; the list in default text. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ComingSoonState is a component with fixed "Coming soon" wording, the badge read as part of the heading, and a highlights list. On Android it composes existing parts: MonarchEmptyState has no slot for a badge or a list, so they sit above and below it, and the badge is read just before the title. The app supplies all the words, so Monarch ships no strings for it. iOS shares the recipe approach.
accessibility: TalkBack reads the badge, then the title and message of MonarchEmptyState, then the list, in that order.
The action is a MonarchButton with a 48dp touch target.
Nothing is conveyed by color alone: "Coming soon" is written.
edgeCases: Do not put a Notify me action without a way to keep the promise.
Keep the list short; it scrolls with the screen.

examples.title: A planned tab
examples.template:
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space3)) {
    MonarchBadge(text = {{badge}}, tone = MonarchTone.Info)
    MonarchEmptyState(
        title = {{title}},
        message = {{description}},
        icon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.Clock, contentDescription = null) },
        actions = { MonarchButton(text = {{action}}, onClick = {}) },
    )
    MonarchText(text = "\u2022 " + {{highlights.0}})
    MonarchText(text = "\u2022 " + {{highlights.1}})
    MonarchText(text = "\u2022 " + {{highlights.2}})
}
examples.code:
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space3)) {
    MonarchBadge(text = "Coming soon", tone = MonarchTone.Info)
    MonarchEmptyState(
        title = "Status pages",
        message = "Publish a page that shows your uptime and incident history.",
        icon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.Clock, contentDescription = null) },
        actions = { MonarchButton(text = "Notify me", onClick = {}) },
    )
    MonarchText(text = "\u2022 " + "A public page on your own domain")
    MonarchText(text = "\u2022 " + "Incident updates by email")
    MonarchText(text = "\u2022 " + "Ninety days of uptime history")
}
